Fumadocs was created because I wanted a more customisable experience for building docs, to be a docs framework that is not opinionated, a "framework" that you can break.
Fumadocs is built from layers: a headless core, a content source, and a UI on top. You can use them together, or replace any of them.

On smaller screens, the table of contents collapses into a popover bar with a progress circle.
The default layout. A sidebar with your page tree, the article in the middle and the table of contents on the right.
Each heading becomes a tick on the right edge of the page. Hover the ticks, and the minimap unfolds into a full table of contents.
The page sits in an inset panel on a card surface, with a table of contents that rolls the active heading in as you scroll.
Every page gets a table of contents generated from its headings. The active headings follow your scroll position, and a thin path traces the depth of each section.

entry.notes: Search dialog (⌘K) on the hero page. open/ = the real open animation at 60 fps (overlay fade-in + dialog-in, 300 ms). Each state = settled result list after typing one more character (hold each for a 16th = 6 frames). dialog.png = dialog only (alpha, incl. its shadow); backdrop.png = overlay colour only (the real overlay also has backdrop-filter, see boxes.overlay.backdropFilter; blur behind.png yourself); behind.png = the page under the dialog. Caret is hidden; boxes.caret gives where it would be. The first row is active by default; ArrowDown moves the highlight.
